title: 1775: the Patriots take the forts
text: The royal government loses its grip. Patriot leaders carry off the arms in Charleston, the Crown's forts at Charlotte and Johnson are given up without a fight, and in the backcountry the first bloodshed ends in a truce and then a Patriot march that breaks the Loyalist camps.

title: 1776: the fort holds, the Cherokee war
text: The palmetto fort on Sullivan's Island drives off the British fleet in June, and Breach Inlet stops the landing. The Cherokee war opens on the western frontier in July; results of the August fights are disputed.

title: 1777: a gap in the list
text: The Archives list has no action for 1777. The one thing read for the year is the end of the Cherokee war: the treaty of 20 May 1777 gives up the Lower Towns' lands.

title: 1778: one entry
text: The list has one entry for the year, the capture of privateers at Charleston on 19 Jun. Nothing read says who took them.

title: 1779: Prevost's move
text: Moultrie beats a British detachment on Port Royal Island in February. In May Prevost's army reaches the Charleston lines and withdraws when Lincoln hurries back. In June Lincoln's attack at Stono Ferry is repulsed; the sources differ on how to score it.

title: 1780: Charleston falls, then the partisan war
text: The British besiege Charleston and Lincoln surrenders on 12 May. Tarleton wins at Monck's Corner, Lenud's Ferry and the Waxhaws, and Cornwallis routs Gates at Camden in August. Local Patriot partisans (Sumter, Marion, the Over-Mountain men) win at Huck's Defeat, Musgrove Mill, Black Mingo, Kings Mountain, Tearcoat Swamp and Fish Dam Ford; Sumter is beaten at Fishing Creek.

title: 1781: Cowpens
text: On 17 Jan Morgan beats Tarleton at Cowpens. Playback ends here; the later actions are loaded as data only.

title: Where things stood on 17 January 1781
text: The British hold Charleston and the posts inland; Patriot partisans hold the swamps and the backcountry, and Morgan's win at Cowpens has opened Greene's campaign. Who held which place is drawn from the control rows, several of them low confidence.
